name: Ladder (dip-buyer), 5-minute BTC
one_liner: The same dip-buying ladder on super-short 5-minute data: buys on small 0.5–3% dips, sells at +1–2.5%, stops at −2–4%. Thousands of tiny trades.
how_it_works: Same staircase idea as the 1-hour version, but the steps are much closer together because 5-minute candles move less. Closer steps mean the orders fill constantly — that is the problem: every fill pays a small fee, and thousands of tiny fees eat the account.

params.name: When it buys
params.plain: When price falls to 0.5%, 1%, 2% or 3% below the recent highest price. Four steps, each with its own money.
params.why: On 5-minute data the moves are tiny, so steps are tiny — but that also makes it buy very often.

params.name: When it sells (profit)
params.plain: At +1%, +1.5%, +2% or +2.5% above each buy price.
params.why: Small goals match the small 5-minute moves.

params.name: When it cuts losses (stop)
params.plain: At −2% or −4% below each buy price.
params.why: The brake, twice as big as the win. It needs to win more than twice as often as it loses — it didn't.

params.name: Buy again after a win
params.plain: After a profitable sell, waits for a 0.75% dip and buys again with the same money.
params.why: Recycles the money — which multiplies the number of fills, and therefore the fees.

params.name: Only in calm markets
params.plain: It compares the average price of the last 50 candles with the last 100. If they drift apart more than 1%, it treats it as a 'trend' and stops.
params.why: The same storm filter as the 1-hour version, but more permissive (1% instead of 0.2%) — so it trades more often.

params.name: Why this page exists
params.plain: It is the fee warning of this course.
params.why: 16,000 tiny trades, $15,000+ in fees on a $100,000 account, profit factor 0.59. Fees, not strategy, killed it.
